utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know what the Territorial Defence was planning or how it functioned. I don't know that. There was not a single public checkpoint. But as for possible preparations for an attack, that's something else. Those were the regular plans of the Territorial Defence which is how it was supposed to function under certain circumstances. But I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, below that, Beco, the same individual we discussed earlier, that's the secretary of the secretariat I believe as you described him, he's discussing what seems to be or at least translated for us, Mr. Sejmenovic, the republic Crisis Staff. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. This is a Crisis Staff organised by area, by zone. It was organised according to zones. So that it was the zone Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's what the RKS stands for, correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Because that was the term that the TO used. In the way it functioned, it was split up into zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Down how many zones were or who the members of these regional or zone Crisis Staffs were, on or about May 2nd, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. You should ask someone from the TO, who was part of the TO then.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In any event, you were familiar that that Crisis Staff existed for some time prior to May 2nd, 1992. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, there was a Territorial Defence. It existed. It was ordered by the republican staff of the TO to begin preparing for defence. How they were acceded, well, there is a procedure. And I really do not know the details. I know the term, the organisational term, that it should be organised on the basis of zones. How many zones there were, how they were linked up, I really do not know. I would tell you gladly if I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Maybe you could help me with this detail, why would Beco propose that money be given for gas so that Alic and Koza can move a lot, and because they have been using their own gas, in essence, petrol, during some of their work?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't know. Really.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if this Koza that he's referring to here, do you know if that's actually the individual who we've referenced before as Kole or Kolina's group, who happened to be the leader of a paramilitary group that was operating and located in the Prijedor Municipality on or about April through July of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Kole, if you're referring to him, he was in the TO. Alic, there was also an Alic in the Territorial Defence. Well, the term "paramilitary formation," it is a relative term. It is a paramilitary formation for the Serbs. And for us, it was Territorial Defence. And it was a regular formation for us. Therefore, to make things clear...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, if you turn, sir, on the next page, 344 of your B/C/S version, on the centre of that page, there's a meeting that's held prior to May 10th, 1992. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right above that. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Under what number? Are you referring to number 4?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The whole section there that appears on page 344, prior to the date of May 10th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. Meaning, a meeting was held. Conclusions were brought. And in the meanwhile, a discussion went on in respect of any other business. Any other business included a discussion on four items, four conclusions were adopted. One, tomorrow to set up a zone Crisis Staff [Methods of work of the RKS.] Two, there was no fuel for the fire brigade, the fire brigade had no fuel, no gasoline. Three, Bahonja: The staff must have the exact number of men and the methods of work. Problem: Here we can swear that this supraparty, body, and that we should act along those lines. What is reaches going on air and into the city, and then in other forms as well. The aim is to preserve everyone's life."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Four, Kemo: "Please exclude me from further work. My health is not well, is not good enough and I have a family problem." And then it goes on to say: "Not accepted."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, directing your attention following this on page 343, which is the continuation of the May 10th, 1992, meeting, can you read for us, please, the first and second full sentence on that page which seems to be missing from the English translation, Your Honour. So we're going to ask the witness to read that. Starting with the word --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The question of weapons in the case of citizens that are not giving them up and are not working, Suljo: On Monday, the military police will be clothed." He's probably referring to the military police or the war police.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir. Are you on page 343?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you, sir, on page 343 of the B/C/S text?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've found the page 343 now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It follows from the May 10th, 1992, meeting, and I would ask you to read the first two full sentences. I think the first word starts with "treba" or "treba vidjeti". If you can read that for us.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My apologies. I will read slowly because it is not very legible. Some parts are easily read. "We must see the degree of sincerity of the other side. We have made the greatest amount of concessions. We have disobeyed the republic, because we said that we would counter this in a democratic fashion."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the reference to that is, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot be quite sure, but I believe that what is being said, that we did not organise TOs on the basis of the republic staff from Sarajevo's orders. But we put this off given the circumstances we were in. We tried to prolong this time, to wait and to try to have talks with the Serb authorities. Perhaps this is referring to the fact the TO insignia were not put on -- given to provocations. It can mean many things. I'm not quite sure which.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You're at the meeting, weren't you? If you look a little further down the page, it identifies a person by the name of Sejmenovic. Do you remember as you sit here, sir, being at a meeting with these people and having these discussions?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the basis of what I have read so far and what you have asked me about so far and skimmed through, it seems to me that this refers to some of the meetings that I attended, given the context of these minutes. It seems to me that these were those meetings, although these meetings were quite similar amongst each other, and it's difficult to distinguish between the one or the second or third meeting. This name here I think, Sejmenovic, that this refers to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to that, sir, do you know who kept these minutes? Do you know if it was a Serb, a Muslim, or a Croat who kept the minutes of these meetings?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. At these meetings were predominantly people of non-Serb ethnicity, but there were Serbs also, but who kept records, I really cannot remember. I can note that the person was not very literate from what I can see how the records were kept. But I don't know who it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I have a couple questions about different parts of this page on the B/C/S version 343. And I'm going to ask you to read it if I may because your name does appear on it, and then I'd like to see what it is you say in response to that. Can you first please read the remainder of that page as you've already started.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I had allegedly -- the part saying Sejmenovic and the colon?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, immediately before that, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I just interrupt for a moment. Mr. Sejmenovic, I have to recall, first of all, and you said this in the beginning, that it's in principle your duty to answer all the questions, and you do it under the solemn declaration. On the other hand, I don't know what will happen now under the cross-examination. But just to be on the safe side in this case, in your safe side, in your interests, I have to recall that it is, of course, also your right not to answer those questions where you have reasonable grounds to believe that this could be amount to self-incrimination. Do you understand this admonition?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand what you're saying, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's just in your own interest. So please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So sir, you read for us on page 343 the first two sentences of that page. I'm just asking you to proceed and read the entire page up until and including what has been attributed as comments made by you, relating to approximately May 10th, 1992 as best as we can see.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So -- shall I read out what I said?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No. If you can just continue with --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To continue, all right. Thank you. "So we decided to dissipate the Republic because we said that we would oppose in a democratic way." Well, this I can't read very well. Two words I cannot read. "One, restriction in these concessions exist. They are not giving 12 policemen to walk around Kozarac without insignia. "One concession, this is only one concession, and they are not giving it to us. As regards Lisbon, they are giving nothing. Some officers from Banja Luka, from the Banja Luka Corps, do not wish to remain. And there has been a rift. It is positive that the impression gained was that we were not prepared, but they themselves were in fear. And therefore, they are in a hurry to present an ultimatum." Something along those lines. That is what is written, I think. Shall I go on reading? "Kemo F.: What would have happened if we hadn't gone yesterday? They would have held a meeting. And they would have probably carried out the action. But then we got five days, five extra days. "Hankic: You're proceeding from the fact that you're protecting the region of Banja Luka, the president of which is Mirza. As regards Mirza" -- this, I cannot read. It's illegible. "We will be saved if the entire area is -- rises. They know that they are ruling. Mirza does not allow authority to be divided. Their authority must be respected. They will come by force and accept authority and will remain in Kozarac. "Ilijaz: Not to interrupt." This is something I cannot read. It's not legible. "Sivac: The main staff of the BH TO exists in Prijedor, and Kozarac is member of that staff in Prijedor." "Husein: I would be happy, I suppose, if this were true. If someone were to come to disarm the police today, I wonder where the command is." "Sejmenovic: There was a public call to the army officers to abandon the ranks of the JNA. These people linked up," and it seems that it says "and now they are contacting amongst themselves and doing their job. No one is contesting the work of the negotiating group, and it should be continued."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know there's more, sir, but I want to ask you a couple questions.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know there's more from, sir, and we are going to discuss that. I'd like just at this point ask you a couple questions. On the first paragraph it discusses the Lisbon talks. Were you familiar on or about May of 1992 what the negotiations were at Lisbon?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the details. I think that these were negotiations conducted by the Sarajevo officials under the sponsorship of the international community. There were negotiations to resolve the crisis in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Why does this individual -- to the best of your knowledge, since apparently you were at the meeting, why does this individual believe that it is positive that the other side presumably "thinks we are unprepared"? Do you have any idea what they were referencing there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Could it be that they were telling the people who were at this meeting that "we're fooling the other side into thinking we're unprepared, but in reality we are prepared. We have our TO set up. We have all our weapons and armaments. We even have our uniforms that were brought in." Could it be that at all, sir, that there was a greater state of preparedness than that as you've previously described?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, sir. I know that there was a tremendous fear prevailing then. I know that much. And one tried at every cost to avoid clashes. And one tried, if the Serb army were to attack, that those parts of the TO should avoid a massacre. And we also hoped that at the state level or the state itself, or the international community would come up with a solution because this seemed possible and probably on the basis of the news we heard. What exactly happened during those negotiations, I do not know. I know that we had in -- before us a force and an experience that held us in fear. What this person had in mind when he said that, I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know the individual who appears a couple names before you, Mr. Hankic? Do you know who that is?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who Mr. Hankic is. You already asked me. If I saw the person, I might recognise him, but the surname means nothing to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When he's referencing "Mirza" there, do you know which Mirza he's referencing?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mirza Mujadzic, president of the party. This is reflected in the sentence, and it is obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I thought so, too. But I didn't want to be presumptuous. It states there that "Mirza did not allow the powers to be divided." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: My question to you is it true, as Mr. Hankic said, that Mirza, the leader of the SDA at that time "refused to allow the powers to be divided in the Prijedor Municipality"? You were at the meeting. Did you speak up later and say: "It's not true, Mirza did not disallow us to divide the powers, in fact, he always was willing and cooperative and made all sorts of concessions to the SDS, regarding these offices or powers?"

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, this is not records from a party meeting. There were people from different parties there and of different ethnicities. I believe that there were members of other ethnic groups also there. And everyone was entitled to say his piece, to say that if someone was working well or not working well. I cannot go into all of this. This is what this person thought, and this is what he said, if we are to believe the records. And this is what the person believed. The aim of this was not to discuss things that you are asking me about.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm just curious to see if I can refresh your recollection of this. But your comment there, it talks about resignations of officers, et cetera, from the former JNA or from the JNA. Do you recall making that statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that the leadership of BH, its presidency composed of all ethnicities, called, invited the officers of the JNA to place themselves on the side of BH. If that is what you are referring to. And a number of officers were designated and obeyed this. And this was the position and call of the authorities of BH, and this is a well-known thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you: The number of officers who designated or obeyed this, were they Serbian or were they Muslim ethnicity who followed the order of the federal institution which they belonged, namely, the JNA, or do you know?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were Serb officers, Croat officers, and Muslim officers. And later on, there was a general -- one of them became a general during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You mention here the presidency which was composed of all ethnicities. The presidency you're referring to is the presidency of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help us because you mention that: When did Alija Izetbegovic declare that he was -- declared it a War Presidency. Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As you sit here, sir, being a member of the parliament representing the Prijedor Municipality, you have no idea when the leader of your party, the SDA, who was president at that time decided to call a War Presidency? You have no idea when it happened? In 1991, 1992, 1993? Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While I was in the BH parliament, this was not proclaimed. I believe in March or February or March 1992, I was in Sarajevo for the last time at a parliament session. And it hadn't been proclaimed then. So in the period while I could go to Sarajevo and attend the meetings there, as far as I can remember, this was not proclaimed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And thank you for clarifying that you left in February or March of 1992, the parliament. But did you hear from the radio, because I know you shared a lot about what you heard from the SDS side and a lot of what you heard on the radio and the television, I suppose. Did you hear at any time any proclamation or any announcement or declaration that Alija Izetbegovic is creating a War Presidency, prior to April of 1992? Did you ever hear that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that it was proclaimed, but I don't remember when. Something -- I think that something like that was heard, but I don't remember when.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Back to the JNA and the officers who left the JNA, is it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. May we have a break of half an hour now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for your understanding. The trial stands adjourned until 5.45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Sejmenovic. Quickly, a question on the material that was provided under your name on this document on page 343. Is it true, sir, that the officers from the JNA who left and came to Kozarac were, in fact, a gentleman by the name of Sead Cirkin, correct, who was a captain? Was he one of those officers?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, Sead Cirkin was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And he was one of those officers that you were referencing in the comments that are attributed to you on page 343 of Exhibit D7A and B respectfully?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. Sead Cirkin was in the JNA. He was in the war in Croatia, and when that war was over, he came home because he is from Kozarusa, as far as I can remember. He was wounded in the leg in the war in Croatia. And he went to recuperate in Kozarusa. His leg was all bandaged up. I was probably referring to Cirkin, although there were very few active-duty JNA officers in Kozarac. I don't know the exact number, but probably two or three.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know if another one was one by the name of Selimbegovic, who was a former JNA officer who quit and then joined ranks in Kozarac?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what the other two were called. I know about Cirkin, and I know that he was in the town of Kozarac itself. How he fitted into the whole picture, I don't know. I don't know the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may just continue with document, Exhibit D7B and A respectively, I may just highlight some of it in the interests of time, if I can direct your attention to the very next page, page 342, and the gentleman identified as Beco, I'd like to know because it's not translated, or I don't have it, what it is exactly that he says there. Again, that's on the B/C/S version, page 342, top right corner.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Beco: Tomorrow, we have to know from --"

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I need to interrupt. I'm sorry, Mr. Sejmenovic. My question really relates to the very last entry by this gentleman, Beco, towards the bottom of the page. You're welcome to read the whole thing, but my question is only with respect to that.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "As long as the people have weapons, they will not recognise the authorities." That's what it says here.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you have any idea, sir, having been at this meeting since it follows the comments being attributed to you on the previous page, what Beco was referring to when he made that statement?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't say exactly what he was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we can go to the next page, sir, page 341 of the B/C/S text, if you can just identify for me the date, and then I'll ask you some questions on that.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date here is very unclear. It says 4, 3, and 5, 1992. So I really don't know what date it is. Is it the 4th of May, 1992? Don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right. Maybe you could help me: Do you know of these meetings that you can see here, the various people similar to the people in the meeting in which you attended, do you know if, in fact, they met at any time as early as March 4th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: There's also a 5 written above the 3. Would it be fair to say that indeed, this is a meeting that occurred on or about May 4th, 1992? Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible, but I'm not sure. Because the date is not stated clearly, so I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And paragraph 3 of that, and for the Court and for the record, I believe the English translation appears on the English text with -- bearing the number 323 on the top right-hand corner. Can you read paragraph 3 for us from that page.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here under 3: "Report on the stay of members of the KS TO, and the SUP, and the proposal for a checkpoint on the main road."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, what checkpoint they are referring to there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what this date is exactly. I know that in early May, the Serbian army set up a checkpoint and brought a tank on to the main road. Whether it refers to that, I don't know. I simply can't answer this. I know that they talked about this, that the representatives of Kozarac asked for that tank to be removed because it was facing the direction of Kozarac. And some talks about this were held. And later on, an order came from Prijedor for the tank to withdraw. However, I can't say anything specific about this because I'm not sure what it's about.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Below that, I think if you see the reference to Mr. Cirkin, that he should take over the RKS, do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the middle of the page or near the bottom?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Right in the middle of the page where there seems to be a question mark in the B/C/S text. See the question mark on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Medunjanin: I propose, if Cirkin is accepted, that he should take over the RKS.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if Mr. Cirkin agreed and that he did take over the RKS, or "S" as you say?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you can follow on that same page, 341, the very last entry, it seems to be comments attributed to Mr. Cirkin.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And for the Court, I think the text appears on the following page, page 322.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you read what it says there, sir.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "Cirkin: To get to work, call on all R. officers."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know what the "R. officers" stands for? Reserve officers, could it be?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possible. Possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who does Mr. Cirkin refer to as R. officers? Do you think at that time, having left the JNA, does he mean the JNA officers or officers from a different entity?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On the following page of that document, sir, page 340 on the B/C/S text, there seems to be a conclusion. And it appears on 322 of the English text. Can you tell me what the conclusion reads, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Conclusion: For Hamdija Kahrimanovic to be coopted in the Kozarac Territorial Defence staff."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know who this individual is?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard about Hamdija Kahrimanovic, but I don't know him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On the top of that page, 340, there seems to be another individual whose name I can't make out. Sujo. Do you see that under numeric number 2, or Sujo?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. It's possible that it's Suljo, or maybe Sudo.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That individual seems to be proposing four men to form an information group, Memic, Saric, Mujagic, and Jasin Fazlic? Is that what it seems to indicate there?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Bahonjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sorry, that wasn't translated. Thank you. Was this the same Jasin Fazlic who was identified earlier in the minutes or in this document D7A who was accused of provoking or carrying out acts of provocation with Hasan and Didin? Do you know if that's the same Fazlic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I can direct your attention, sir, to the next page, and we'll get to, I think, where you made some comments. But on page 339, can you read for me, sir, what seems to be written under the name of Pasic, which is towards the second half of the document?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Pasic: I agree with the discussion and with the comrades. We are under occupation. The occupation authorities are imposing their control over us." Then there is something that's illegible. And in the next row, it says: "To accept it." And then another illegible word. "Time or war. The establishing of a municipality is nothing." I can't read the first word here, but then it goes on to say: "As for these insignia," and then this is also illegible. And they say that "this is an order from BL. It seems that they are willing to give up their symbols if we go for a war, many will die. But a municipality is not the solution. They claim that the army will not get involved. We must try" and it's possible it says here "to try to gain time to engage in tactics."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On the next page, sir, page 338 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: On the next page, sir, page 338, I'd like you to read the text where your name appears with comments attributed to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I believe, Your Honour, that appears on page 319 of the English text.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you start from the beginning of the page, sir.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "Sejmenovic:" --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you read the paragraph right before that as well for us. I apologise for interrupting you.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "If someone attacks me," and this part is illegible, an illegible word, "I will," well, it looks like "scratch him with my ring," but I'm not sure about this at all. "They" and then there is another illegible word, "that in Kozarac there are thousands of weapons. In Svrakino Selo near Sarajevo, they had agreed about everything, and they had handed them in. They collected them and took them to Serbia. First, it's the police, then it's the turn of the Territorial Defence, and then of the citizenry. "The children in school are saying that Kozarac will pay for the communities." Then it says: "Sejmenovic:"

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Before you read what you read here, Mr. Sejmenovic,.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Before you read what is attributed to you, at any time, sir, having been at this meeting or do you recall ever a discussion that there were thousands of weapons that were being discussed?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that. I don't remember, and also this part is illegible. I don't know who some of these sentences refer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall at all whether there was a discussion in early May that the children were still attending school, even after the takeover, as seems to be the indication by whoever made this comment? Do you remember that discussion?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The children went to school for another week at most after the takeover of power. I've already talked about that. In Prijedor, it was still possible to go on, somehow, up to mid-May. I don't remember now -- I don't remember anything more about it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Help me with this: In 1992, when did the grammar schools close for the summer, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you just proceed and please read the comments that are attributed to you, sir, on that page 338.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Sejmenovic: I can see two options. Without insignia or with insignia on the police. But the question arises of the safety of people. Who will defend them after the disarming if we hand over our weapons?" Then there are two illegible words. And two illegible words. And then it says: "Many will suffer if we" -- something illegible --" time, we have to invest everything. I'm not in favour of leaving people without protection. Rather, I am in favour of at least trying to defend ourselves."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you, sir, remember making -- I think that's the end of the comments attributed to you. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you, sir, remember making these statements and actually telling the people that you would rather you tried to defend yourselves?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you at any time, sir, take the position of the items that are raised in the comments that are attributed to you on page 338?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's possible that I took part in some discussions, but this was an area I did not participate in actively, because I was neither a member of the police, nor of the Territorial Defence, so that I rarely took the floor at these meetings. And I was not part of the structures that were dealing with these issues directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Having reviewed this document, can you tell us which structure this was, whether it was the structure of the police or the structure of the Territorial Defence or a combination of both?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there were both, people from the municipalities, the Territorial Defence, the police, the party. I was present as the deputy at the republic level.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Lower on that page 338, there's a Bahonjic, who is also essentially quoted, or commented about things that he said. Could you read that to me. It's on the same page that your name appears, apparently at the same meeting in which you attended. Can you read that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here: "Bahonjic: If Kozarac intends to hand over their weapons, let them do so. The people from" probably "Jakupovici," and then the next part is illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Does it look like "ce ubite" [sic]?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "With both, or with eyes," and then let Kozarac -- doesn't say anything further.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir, I interrupted you. After the area or the town that they referenced, Jakupovici, what does it say? Can you read that for us? That the people from Jakupovici will what?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here, at least that's what it looks like to me, "kill" either POV or PAR, but the copy is not completely legible. And then it says either "with O-B-A" or with O-K-A, meaning both or eyes, and then it says: "Let Kozarac."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall in a meeting in which you were present whether Mr. Bahonjic actually made that statement regarding the people from Jakupovici?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, if the incident that occurred on May 24th, 1994, at the main road leading from Banja Luka to Prijedor whether there was an incident in the town that's located near the town that's referenced by Mr. Bahonjic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the information on the radio, we heard about two incidents, one in Kozarusa and one in Jakupovici. In Jakupovici on the road. Jakupovici is a very broad area. There is upper or Gornji Jakupovici or lower or Donja Jakupovici. A group of hamlets on one side and a group of hamlets on the other side of the Prijedor/Kozarac/Banja Luka Road. The incident where they allegedly attempted to stop some tanks, that's what I think happened, this took place in Jakupovici, according to the information we heard on the radio or from the Territorial Defence, and this happened on the road in Jakupovici. Whether it refers to this or not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And as you sit here having been at the meeting, you have no recollection of that discussion at all. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, these are minutes from a meeting. The meeting went on. There were discussions, and the person taking the minutes summarised what was said in a few sentences. I don't remember every detail. There were several meetings and they are all very similar to each other. Similar topics were discussed. I could tell you but I can't improvise. I remember some things that were said, and I don't remember others.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The military convoy that was attacked on May 24th, 1992, at the checkpoint at Jakupovici, did it strike you as being odd that there was a discussion at a meeting where Mr. Bahonjic actually described what the citizens would do from that area if they had to surrender their arms?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm. This sentence is not clear to me. I don't remember anyone saying that someone should be killed because they are or are not handing in their weapons. I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I may just try to quickly get through this document at the very least, on page 336 of the B/C/S text, towards the bottom of that text, sir, Beco again is quoted or words are attributed to this Beco. Can you read to us what at the bottom or near the bottom of that page Beco had apparently said at this meeting, which, I believe, if you turn to the page prior would have been on May 5th, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On the previous page, it does say the 5th of May, 1992. And Beco says here: "The SDS is conducting negotiations exclusively with the SDA, and not with the local commune. I propose that we wait for tomorrow's meeting of the SDA and to see what their standpoint is." And finally: "To hold a meeting of all the citizens and let them express their views."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So does this, sir, at all refresh your recollection as to whether there were many and, in fact, multiple meetings that the SDS called and had with the SDA during the time immediately after the takeover on April 30th, 1992, and it was not, sir, as you claim the only meeting on May 1st, and then the subsequent meeting in mid-May 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the last meeting with the SDS, and I spoke about that here. As for this meeting, the one Beco is referring to here, I think this refers to an SDA meeting at which standpoints were to be reached which were then to be discussed with the SDS. One such meeting was held at Hambarine, and that might have been in the first week of May or thereabouts. I remember at that time individuals tried to establish contact, and it's possible that a meeting was formally held with the SDS at that time. But I was not a member of any delegation as far as these meetings are concerned. What I do know is that I was tasked with being present at one such meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And if I can direct your attention, sir, to the next page, page 335, and the centre of the page seems to bear a date of May 6th, 1992. Would you be able to read the second and third entries that are made on that date.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 2: "The replacement of the existing members of the KS".

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: What does that mean, "KS"? Means Crisis Staff, right? We interpreted it several times here --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could mean Crisis Staff. It could also mean the staff command. I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And the next paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "To go to a meeting with an announcement --" I can't read this word here. It's illegible to me. But underneath, it says: "Conclusions or conclusion" or something similar. And then possibly "proposals," but I'm not sure. And then, under number 4, it says: "Other business".

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, tell me if you, during that time period in question, approximately May 6th, 1992, were you advocating that the citizens refuse to surrender the arms? Or were you in favour of them surrendering the arms?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have a firm standpoint on that because I did not have complete information about the capacity and the possibilities of the Territorial Defence and everything else. What was clear to me was that in other areas, non-Serb areas had come under attack, regardless of whether they were armed or not. And my standpoint was that we should simply try everything, negotiate, send delegations, not provide any pretexts to them. But personally, I was afraid that we would be attacked regardless of what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the details, I don't remember enough to go into details.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I understand that. That's why I'm going to direct your attention to page 333 where your name appears on the bottom of the page, and it continues with comments that are attributed to you on page 332, and maybe this will help refresh your recollection as to what your position was on or about May 6th, 1992, in connection with the arms. If you could read it out loud, because I don't know that we have the --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Sejmenovic: Some areas will be resolved through agreements." Then there is an illegible word. And then it says -- no, this other word is also illegible. Then it says: "We will not give up our weapons. There are no guarantees for the people from their government."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Does that, sir, refresh your recollection as to what your position was on or about May 6th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't be quite sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As you sit here, sir, do you have any recollection whatsoever of ever having taken the position that's reflected on the comments attributed to you? Or you just don't remember?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already said, I simply don't remember. I see the text. I see what has been put down as the summary of what people said. But I cannot remember what standpoint I advocated.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you recall as you sit here, sir, what areas were going to be resolved by or through agreements, as it is attributed -- I think it would be fair, if you just look, you're welcome to look at the entire document. Immediately before that, there's a discussion of the Lisbon Agreement, I'm not sure if you're referencing that, but perhaps you could help us out with that.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I cannot remember. I know that this process was underway, that there were delegations in Banja Luka. But what this was about, I can't recall at present.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask if the Court would please have the usher show you Exhibit SK46A and B. Really, just B, the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And just so the record is clear, that's a document from Dr. Donia. I think we identified them as the "SK" documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But just let me take the opportunity, just for clarification, the Judges have discussed the issue of possible time limits. Of course, it's free for the Defence to decide how to use the time, but the time is not unlimited. And therefore, we decided to impose a time limit to finalise the cross-examination no later than tomorrow at the end of the hearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, we have an idea from Defence Exhibit 7A and B what seems to be your thought process or at least your feelings in May of 1992. Now, SK46B, if you look at that, and I direct your attention to page 2 of that which has the ERN number 00633866, I believe. And this is a document that's already in evidence, and there's a comment attributed to Dr. Stakic on or about May 9th, 1992. Can you read for me, sir, where it says there where in fact Dr. Stakic, on that date, apparently said: "Peace must be maintained at all costs." Do you see that written there, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it says here: "Milomir Stakic - from the 30th of April, 1992" and then in the Municipality of Prijedor here, from the constitution of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina is implemented, and the because in accordance with the constitution. Where new laws have not been enacted, the old ones will be implemented. The next month or two are the most critical until the funds that have now been established are replenished. Peace has to be maintained at all costs, and the economy has to be revived. Committee of five members with Savanovic at its head has been established to receive the soldiers coming back from the front. General mobilisation is obligatory, and the Serbs are required to respond to the callup."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, your position, on or about May of 1992, was not one of peace; it was one to arm the citizens. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think there's some limitation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I saw Your Honour looking at me. Can I stand up. First of all, there was no question as far as I saw. The witness was asked to read the document, and then a comment is effectively being made. But secondly, I was going to say if the Defence case is that this witness actually was responsible for arming the Muslim population or in some way was involved, then it's something that should be put to him so Your Honours can see how he deals with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's only fair, and I would ask the Defence to refrain from comments as they were made in the last question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sejmenovic, on the page that your name appears last on -- I'm done with SK46A and B, sir. Directing your attention, sir, to Exhibit D7A and B, specifically pages 332 and 333, again, sir, you don't know or do you have any recollection of whether these agreements that you reference involved the Lisbon agreements that are referenced merely six lines above that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is this page 332?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I apologise. I don't remember. And I can't explain with any certainty what this was about. This may have been an interpretation of the news report we listened to about this event, but I cannot recall enough to be able to speak about it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Following your comments or the comments that are attributed to you and turning to page 332, there is an individual by the name of Suljo who makes a comment, after others spoke, during the same meeting apparently in which you were in attendance. Can you tell us what he says in that section.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Suljo: We must buy time also on the issue of insignia. But if weapons have to be returned, then there will be a war."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Having been at that meeting, sir, do you remember the individual named Suljo making that statement that's attributed to him?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember these details.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough for me, sir, to just flip through the balance of the pages before you in the B/C/S text and tell me if your name appears anywhere else on these entries?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see my name being mentioned, but I'll go through it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I don't either, Mr. Sejmenovic --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. In July of 1998 in your testimony in the Kovacevic case, you discussed an issue regarding a TV relay at Kozarac. Do you remember generally when and if a TV relay at Kozarac and Lisina was actually captured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please be so kind and as it is custom in this courtroom tell us where you are quoting from? Wednesday, 8 July, 1998?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I wasn't quoting, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You're making reference to testimony in the Kovacevic case.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Page 373, lines 1 through 10, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'm not quoting from that transcript, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just want to understand and have an appreciation of the information you have in connection with the TV relay station. Can you tell me when it was that that TV relay station at Kozarac and Lisina was captured?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember precisely, but it was in the second half of 1991. Because I know that there was a discussion on this in the parliament of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Unfortunately, I cannot tell you with precision.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me who seized the TV relay station and from whom?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What we heard at the time was that some farmers who were near the relay station, who had their farms up there saw, some people in camouflage uniforms carrying weapons who carried out an intervention at the relay station, and the personnel who had been employed there were chased out. And some other persons were brought in. We learned about this event when the TV broadcast was interrupted. So it was evident. Several days later, maybe a day later, I'm not sure any more, the signal of Belgrade television was suddenly received. And after that, Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know, sir, who controlled that TV relay station prior to the attempt to seize it by these unidentified men in camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was information that this was done by the army, but the army did not wear camouflage uniforms at the time. Camouflage uniforms were seen, and this interpretation came from eyewitnesses. Who controlled it previously, I don't know because I was never up there. All I know is that up to that point, we saw broadcasts of Sarajevo television, and sometimes Belgrade or Zagreb television. But from that point on, the TV broadcasts were completely different.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you know why anyone would want to seize a TV relay station?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll try to restate it. Is there anything near the TV relay station that was in existence in 1991, anything near or around the area where this TV relay station was?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you referring to when you say "something" or "anything"? It's a mountain.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll be more specific. Thank you. I understand that it's on the mountain, but was there any barracks there or any military armaments that were being kept near or around the area of the TV relay station, sir?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Near the TV relay station, there was nothing. The relay station was at Lisina. I think that's the name of the peak. And that's part of the mountain of Kozara. Going along the top of Kozara from Lisina towards Mrakovica, JNA barracks and military installations were quite some distance. They were at Mrakovica. I don't think there was anything in the vicinity, not as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were there any, to the best of your knowledge - and I know your limited experience in the military - do you know if there were any military installations near or around the TV relay station in 1991?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any information to the effect that there were any military installations near the TV relay station. I know there were some at Benkovac, and I had some sort of information that near Benkovac, there were other military installations, and allegedly helicopters were able to land there. But none of this was near Lisina, according to the information I had. The JNA sometimes had facilities that people didn't know about, so it's possible that something did exist there, but this is the first time I've heard of anything like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And let me just turn the topic, since we only have about 15 minutes left, on an issue that I'd like to address. You gave a video or you gave a statement that was videotaped that we saw during your direct examination. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With respect to that, sir, I'm a little confused on a couple points. Once you mentioned a Mr. Mutic, I think. And then you mention a Dragan Bozanic. Can you tell me, sir, were you interviewed on more than one occasion?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mutic interviewed me twice, and after that, Bozanic interviewed me once. Mutic was from the local TV station and the Krajina television, and Bozanic was doing it on behalf of Serbian television.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And how far apart was it in terms of time when you gave the first, second, and third interview?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mutic interviewed me once, and after a day or two, a day or two later, I'm not sure exactly. And then three or four days after that, some foreign journalists arrived accompanied by Bozanic, who then conducted the third interview with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned that the interviews that were given by Mr. Mutic or conducted by Mr. Mutic, you were given some instructions, correct, as what to say?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He gave me those instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it fair to say that Mr. Dragan Bozanic did not give you any such instructions?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Bozanic came in, in a hurry, in the room where I was, and put questions, the questions we saw on the tape. He didn't say to me: "You have to answer like this or like that." Simply, he interviewed me and I answered in the way you heard me do, based on the experience I had with the journalist Mutic and in accordance with the situation I was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So at the time that Dragan Bozanic interviewed you, he didn't ask you to answer in any manner; he didn't instruct you how to answer. And during the time that he interviewed you, there were also foreign journalists at the camp and other foreign individuals, if you will. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were no foreign journalists in the room, only journalists of Crna, the Serbian television, and several camp guards who had entered the room and were watching me as I was answering the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We saw some of your interview, or possibly even all of it, with respect to Mr. Bozanic. Do you know whether there is in existence the interviews that you allegedly gave where you read from a written transcript which was given to you by Mr. Mutic? Did you ever see any such video footage of that?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When was the first time, sir, that you retracted the comments that you made on this video by the interview that was made by Mr. Dragan Bozanic, who did not instruct you on what to say? When was the first time that you retracted those comments?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have already been asked this question here. I answered that, and I repeat it now. I don't know what you mean by "retracted." If you would explain this to me, I will then tell you whether I did that or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: All right. If I'm permitted, I'd like to try at least. Sir, if you make a comment, and you don't agree with the comment, later, you would advise someone, "I did not agree to make that comment," or I'm going to retract or disavow myself of the statements I made on TV.

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now I understand. Now, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I can just -- my question to you, sir: When from August 1992, when was the first time that you retracted or disavowed the comments that you made while being interviewed by Mr. Dragan Bozanic?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I understand you now. I said in my statement that I was forced to answer in the way I did, and I did that for the first time in 1993. I said that to a person who was represented a UN commission. I think it was chaired by a gentleman called Cherif Bassiouni or something like that. And a lady came to talk to me in Zagreb. Her name was Ferial Karaci [phoen] or Garaci [phoen]. She was from the UN commission. I made a statement about this. And it's possible that during my interview with her, which lasted for several hours, I think that was the first time I said that. It's possible I also said that to the representatives of the embassy of Bosnia and Herzegovina. I'm not sure which came first in chronological order, but I think it was the UN commission that came first. I'm speaking of my interview with them. I don't remember, however, whether this was taken down in writing or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, as you sit here, you don't know whether it was or not. Correct?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure it happened, but I'm not sure whether it was taken down in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Do you remember giving testimony on July 14th, 1998, at pages 713 through 714, where an identical question was asked of you in connection with your retraction or disavowing or contradiction from the statements Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. you made to now claiming that they were given under duress and being asked when was it the first time that you disavowed yourself from those comments? It states, if I may --

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you. I repeat. I remember that this question was put to me and I was very confused by it because retracting a statement means, to me, saying that I did not say that. That's why I was confused when that question was put to me. You, unlike your colleague who asked me that question, you have explained this to me, which is why I can answer you precisely now.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, just to paraphrase, and you tell me if it's right or wrong, I'm just trying to get an understanding, on July 14th, 1998, when asked hen you actually retracted that statement, on line 4 through, I believe, 14 on page 714 of that date, you state, sir, "Answer: During the conversation which I had about my stay in the camp, I believe that this conversation was conducted with one of the investigators of The Hague Tribunal. It was the first time then that I talked about these events, and this is when I spoke about it, about this interview and about the taping." It goes on to state: "Question, if you could remember perhaps the month or a session and what year that you spoke to representatives of the Tribunal and that you took back this statement." "Answer: In 1995, I believe in late 1995, but I'm not sure. It could have even been early 1996." Just so I understand, Mr. Sejmenovic, is it your testimony that you retracted this statement in 1993 or sometime in 1995 or 1996?

utterances.speaker: MEVLUDIN SEJMENOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for representatives of the Tribunal, my first contact with them was when I said it was. In 1993, there was no Tribunal. In Zagreb, there was an office of that UN commission, and there was a lady whose name I have told you, and then I was interviewed. We spoke in the consulate of Bosnia and Herzegovina in Zagreb. The address was Novakova [phoen] Street. I think it was Number 9. This was not with Tribunal investigators. My first conversation with Tribunal investigators was detailed, at least as far as the things they asked me. They didn't ask me about everything, and I told them this then. But if you say: "When was the first time in general that I retracted this, regardless of whether it was the Tribunal or somebody else?" Then it would be this UN commission, and I still have the visiting card of the person who interviewed me. Not only me, she interviewed a number of people who were arriving in Zagreb at the time. But nothing happened after these interviews. Nobody called me or asked me about anything. Then the Tribunal investigators came, and that was when I had the formal interview with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think I understand. Sir, I'm going to ask you, and I should probably tell the Court I'm going to move to a totally different area in connection with the minutes of the extraordinary session of Prijedor Municipal Assembly held on the 14th of February, 1992. Mr. Sejmenovic was present apparently at the meeting. I don't know if the Court wants me to start with the questioning now or if it would be an appropriate time. I know we have five, six minutes left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: After the impression of today's discussion of one document, I'm afraid we would sit here until 10.00. So therefore, I think it's more appropriate to start this issue, this new issue, tomorrow. The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow, 2.15.
